synopsis: Chapter 9 and the glossary describe robust or worst-case optimization as targeting the worst stratum or a high percentile rather than average performance, protecting difficult conditions such as dust at night [f6988, f14399]. Chapter 9 specifies min-max optimization over strata and says the approach avoids sacrificing weak-stratum performance while favoring stable operating regions [f7329, f7330]. The trade-off is conservatism and a potentially higher nuisance rate [f7331]. Although the approach is described as having lower over-fitting risk, held-out strata remain necessary, and no off-road evidence for robust or worst-case tuning was found [f7332, f7333].

relations.note: Glossary restates Chapter 9's objective and dust-at-night rationale.
Specifies min-max over strata as the worst-case tuning formulation.
Adds preference for stable operating regions to weak-stratum protection.
Adds conservatism and potentially increased nuisance rates as trade-offs.
Adds lower over-fitting risk and the continuing need for held-out strata.
Qualifies the method description with the absence of found off-road evidence.
Adds the min-max formulation to the worst-stratum optimization description.
Restates weak-stratum protection and adds stable operating-region preference.
